findings.finding: The pinned Hugging Face realtime service parses conversation.item.truncate as ConversationItemTruncateEvent.

The pinned websocket router deliberately treats ConversationItemTruncateEvent as no additional server-state mutation after cancellation because client-side playback is considered owner of the unheard tail.

OpenAI Realtime reference semantics define conversation.item.truncate as synchronizing server understanding with client playback, removing server-side text transcript beyond the heard audio boundary, and returning conversation.item.truncated on success.

reconciliation.current_question: Does the HF cancellation/rollback path produce behavior observationally equivalent to OpenAI's heard-boundary server-context truncation despite truncate itself being a no-op?
reconciliation.architectural_implication: HF cannot be credited as drop-in OpenAI-Realtime semantic equivalence at the truncate boundary from source alone. F2 remains viable if its existing authority boundary reconstructs or otherwise proves next-turn context contains no unheard assistant semantics.

highest_information_discriminator.falsifies_drop_in_semantics_if: Any unheard assistant semantic remains in next-turn model context, or truncate success is represented without equivalent heard-boundary state synchronization.
highest_information_discriminator.does_not_falsify_f2_adapter_if: F2 reconstructs authoritative context from its own heard-state boundary and proves the speech server cannot reintroduce unheard/stale semantics.
